threepl.exec

Class Immediate

  • java.lang.Object
    • threepl.exec.Var
      • threepl.exec.Immediate
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    TDEConstants, Constant

    public final class Immediate
extends Var
implements Constant, TDEConstants
    This class represents an immediate mode variable. The variable has a name String, a mode and a Type, which may be complex. If the variable is a module, procedure or function parameter it may have an indirect pointer to another Var, depending on its mode and whether input or output. If the variable is a target mode it will also have an expanded name to ensure that this instance is unique.

    There is an array containing values for all words of the variable. There is also an associated array containing the Type of each word (this array is present for all modes). The values are objects of suitable type for the primitive type (see threepl.parser.Constant.java) -

    • Long for Ptype.INT or Ptype.UINT
    • Boolean for Ptype.LOG
    • String for Ptype.STR
    • Ref for Ptype.PTR (a pointer)
    The following special cases apply -
    • If isInPar is true then this variable is a module, procedure or function input parameter.
    • If isOutPar is true then this variable is a module or procedure output parameter.

      • Immediate

        public Immediate(java.lang.Object[] o,
                 Type[] t,
                 WordSpec ws,
                 SrcLoc loc)
        Construct an immediate variable as a wrapper for a Val. This is used for Val classes assigned to maps or lists as it allows a Ref to be generated for the resulting map or list value. This in turn allows assignment to a field or array map or list entry and also allows a pointer to a map or list entry, or field or array member of an entry, to be generated.
        Parameters:
        o - is the array of primitive values in the associated Val
        t - is the array or primitive types
        ws - is the WordSpec for the Val
        loc - is the source file location

      • getRef

        public Ref getRef(VarNode varnode,
                  SubFieldList sfl,
                  boolean is_val,
                  SrcLoc loc)
        Get a reference to a variable. The reference is generally used for assignment to a variable however the value of a variable can also obtained by starting with the reference. The main information contained in the reference is -
        • a list of words in the variable selected by subscripts or field names
        • a list of primitive types for each word
        • for target variables a list of bit pairs associated with the word list
        • a multi-dimensioned array giving the dimensionality of the reference
        • a type to make sure assignment types match
        • a TDEVar for a target variable
        The varnode argument is used to get any flags associated with the variable occurence (++ or -- flags of the string indirect operator/flag), but it may be null if the reference is being requested in some other context. The subs argument is a list of subscript or field nodes associated with the variable occurence - it may be null. A pointer variable returns a reference to the ultimate variable to which it points.
        Overrides:
        getRef in class Var
        Parameters:
        varnode - is the tree node for the variable occurrence or is null if the reference is not associated with a variable occurrence (used to detect ++, -- or ?)
        sfl - is the list of associated subscript and field nodes after the subscript and field nodes have been evaluated
        is_val - indicates that we want a value rather than a reference
        loc - is the source file location
        Returns:
        the reference to the variable
